Header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Amy (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM); Dr. Priya, Marcus, Sofia, Evan (Lumenix)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, partial): Lumenix is evaluating Redwood for a private deployment with strict EU/US data residency needs. Focus on KMS/HSM options, region pinning, subprocessor visibility, SOC 2/ISO proof, and audit log retention. They requested a bench and KMS escrow options.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Amy: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Amy from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, Jared from our infra team and Nina our CSM are with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Dr. Priya: Hey Amy, doing fine thanks, we are excited to dig in — big agenda for us, lots of compliance constraints so thanks for carving out time.
[00:18] Marcus: Yeah thanks, we'll walk through both legal and tech sides today, but main ask is how we can pin EU data, avoid cross-border processing, and the KMS setup.
[00:25] Amy: Great, on my side we'll cover high level controls, Jared will jump into private deployment and KMS specifics, and Nina will cover onboarding and next steps.
[00:33] Jared: Hi all — quick note, I'll probably mispronounce some things, and our deployer product is the Redwood Dedicated runtime, sometimes we call it 'Dedicate' in notes, apologies if that appears in transcriptions.
[00:44] Sofia: That's fine, clarity on terms is appreciated. For legal: we need subprocessors list, data flow diagrams, and confirmation that EU customer data never leaves region unless explicitly allowed.
[00:55] Amy: Absolutely. We have a subprocessor inventory spreadsheet, I'll share that after the call. It includes cloud infra partners, monitoring, and optional partners. EU region pinning is supported via our Private control plane or Dedicated with region affinity — Jared will explain the mechanics.
[01:10] Jared: Mechanically we support region pinning two ways: 1) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where control plane and inference can be deployed in EU only; or 2) Hosted Dedicated with region affinity — we route requests to pods in eu-west-1 and enforce routing policies. There is a fallback policy that can be turned off if you require hard pinning.
[01:35] Dr. Priya: Fallbacks are a concern, we can't have automatic cross-border failover. Is there an option to disable that fallback entirely?
[01:42] Jared: Yes, for regulated accounts we can disable cross-region fallback; if eu capacity is exhausted requests will queue or return 429s rather than route out of region. There is an SLA tradeoff, we can discuss burst capacity.
[01:57] Evan: What about KV cache and prefix caching — does that ever replicate across regions?
[02:04] Jared: Good question. We keep KV cache scoped to a region instance. We do not replicate customer KV state across regions unless customers opt into multi-region replication. In our private deployment, it's under your network so it never leaves.
[02:20] Marcus: KMS — we need to know if keys can be customer-managed. And HSM / escrow? We have internal requirement for keys under customer control or escrow for recovery.
[02:30] Amy: We support BYOK — bring your own key — via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault). For Private installs, you can use your own KMS over the VPC. For hosted Dedicated we offer a customer KMS workflow where keys are in your account and we use envelope encryption.
[02:47] Dr. Priya: Do you support HSM-backed keys (cloud HSM) and can we have a KMS escrow arrangement?
[02:54] Jared: Yes, cloud HSM-backed keys are supported via the respective cloud provider KMS, e.g., AWS CloudHSM. Escrow is available in our enterprise plan — we can arrange an escrow with a neutral third party. We'll detail options in the security packet.
[03:10] Sofia: For audit logs: retention, tamper-evidence, and exportability are key. We need at least 7 years retention readable by auditors, immutable logs, and SSO access mapping.
[03:21] Nina: On audit logs we store request/response metadata and system logs; customers can configure log export to their SIEM via shipper to a customer-owned logging account. Immutability is handled via append-only storage in the customer's cloud in Private deployments; in hosted modes we have WORM policies and export options.
[03:39] Marcus: Does Redwood keep full request/response payloads? That is, do you store PII in any logs by default?
[03:45] Amy: By default we store minimal metadata and error traces; payloads are not stored unless customers enable full request logging. For Private deployments the default is no payload retention unless you enable args. We'll include default retention policies in the packet.
[03:58] Dr. Priya: How do you handle data erasure requests (GDPR right to be forgotten) across backups and caches?
[04:05] Jared: We have a data deletion playbook: we remove primary data, expire KV cache items, and trigger backup deletion according to retention schedules. For hosted customers we can expedite and confirm deletion; for Private deployments it's in customer control but we provide tooling and scripts. Note that some backups are immutable for a short TTL — we document exact windows.
[04:26] Amy: We will attach the deletion SLA and the backup TTL windows.
[04:29] [05:00] <-- 5 minute mark, quick cross talk -->
[05:10] Marcus: On network segregation — for VPC we assume a dedicated subnet and no public ingress?
[05:16] Jared: Correct. Private requires dedicated subnets, private endpoints, and no public egress unless you configure a NAT. You can also use peering and private link options.
[05:28] Evan: We need SSO and RBAC integrated with our IdP — we use SAML with Okta. Mapping groups to roles is essential.
[05:36] Nina: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls that map to your groups. We'll send role templates.
[05:44] Sofia: Also need separation of duties — some users can see logs but not PII, others can manage keys but not view content. Can that be enforced?
[05:53] Jared: Yes, RBAC is granular: admin, operator, auditor, reader, and custom roles. Key material management actions require an elevated key-admin role.
[06:05] Dr. Priya: On subprocessors, we saw some notes about monitoring vendors and a model-ops partner. We need to know if any model supplier or tokenizer vendor has access to raw customer content.
[06:15] Amy: Our model catalog includes open models and partner models. For hosted modes some third-party logging/observability partners may receive telemetry but not raw content. Any model weights or inference touches are within the runtime — subprocessors don't get customer payloads by default. However we'll provide the inventory and any data flow diagrams to confirm.
[06:37] Marcus: Is there any third party that might see data for model quality or evals?
[06:42] Jared: Only if you opt into a managed eval or human review product — that's an opt-in separate contract. It is not part of normal inference flows.
[06:50] Sofia: Let's talk about cross-border legal risk: Shrems II references keep coming up — do you do onshore proxying or do you rely on SCCs?
[06:58] Amy: We rely on SCCs and other appropriate transfer mechanisms for subprocessors. For customers requiring no transfers we recommend Private or dedicated region-only deployments. We'll include legal language in the contract addendum.
[07:12] Dr. Priya: Encryption at rest — we need to confirm all disk and object storage are encrypted, plus in-transit TLS, and internal service-to-service encryption.
[07:21] Jared: All storage is encrypted at rest using KMS keys; in transit uses TLS 1.2+ currently TLS 1.3 is optional depending on endpoint. Service-to-service connections inside the cluster use mutual TLS when in Private deployments.
[07:35] Evan: What about key rotation — can we enforce rotation schedules and get audit of key usage?
[07:41] Jared: Yes—key rotation can be automated by the customer KMS or scheduled by Redwood if you allow it. All KMS calls are audited and we can export KMS audit logs to your monitoring account.
[07:52] [08:00] <- 8 minute marker ->
[08:05] Marcus: Benchmarks: we want a 100 ms p99 target for short prompts, but we also want burst throughput. How does region pinning affect latency if eu pods are smaller?
[08:17] Jared: Region pinning to eu-west-1 won't add significant network latency beyond regional RT, but capacity constraints matter. If you size dedicated pools in EU we can hit 100 ms p99 for small sequences on select models. Quantization and batching policies affect that too.
[08:34] Amy: Note on quantization: model variants like 8-bit quant might reduce latency and cost but can change output characteristics; we'll run evals.
[08:42] Dr. Priya: For audits, we will need a runbook and access to logs for our auditors — can Redwood provide time-windowed snapshots and attestations?
[08:50] Nina: We provide audit bundles (evidence packs) for SOC2 and ISO audits: config snapshots, logs, change history. For Private, you own logs; we help assemble.
[09:02] Sofia: Can you provide SOC 2 type II report and ISO 27001 certificate?
[09:07] Amy: Yes, we will share certified reports — I'll attach the latest SOC2 type II and ISO cert in the security packet.
[09:15] Marcus: Any limitations around data residency for embeddings? We run semantic search over user content and often embeddings are stored for performance.
[09:24] Jared: Embeddings are treated like any other customer artifact; they can be configured to remain in-region, or stored in your tenant's object store. We recommend storing embeddings in customer-managed buckets in Private setups.
[09:37] Dr. Priya: Regarding incident response, what is your disclosure timeline and access for post-incident forensics?
[09:44] Amy: Standard is 72 hours initial notification for high-severity incidents, then regular updates. For enterprise contracts we offer tighter SLAs and forensic support. We'll include our IR playbook excerpt.
[09:58] [10:00] --- short break (brief side chatter) ---
[10:18] Evan: On contract language, we need to add clauses for hard region pinning, no cross-border fallback, and subprocessor notification windows. Who can own that in Redwood legal?
[10:28] Amy: I'll be the owner and I'll loop in Legal; we'll propose contract language and provide a standard addendum for region pinning.
[10:36] Dr. Priya: Pilot scope — we want a privacy-preserving bench: deploy a trial in EU with BYOK, run 10k token bench, and validate audit log export. Can Redwood do that?
[10:46] Jared: Yes — we can spin up a private VPC deployment in eu-west-1 for a 2-week bench. We'll need a small topology: 2 inference pods, 1 control-plane, and log exporter to your logging account.
[10:58] Marcus: What about cost for bench? We prefer minimal cost, but if we need burst capacity that may be charged.
[11:05] Amy: We'll provide a bench quote; usually we offer a discounted evaluation rate. We'll include cost estimates in follow-up.
[11:12] Nina: I'll coordinate scheduling and requirements and will create a runbook for the bench.
[11:19] [12:00] <- 12 minute marker ->
[12:30] Dr. Priya: One specific ask: can you attest that no human reviewers will see PII without explicit opt-in?
[12:38] Amy: We can attest: human review is opt-in and requires separate contract and controls. By default we do not route content to human reviewers.
[12:46] Sofia: Data residency for backups — are backups replicated to other regions for durability? Any cross-region replication must be opt-in.
[12:55] Jared: Correct, cross-region backup replication is opt-in; durability within region is provided by multi-az replication, not cross-region.
[13:08] Marcus: For monitoring, which managed services are in the subprocessor list? We need names and countries.
[13:14] Amy: We'll share a scannable CSV; minimal set includes log shipping provider, metrics provider, and incident alerting partner — names and country of operation included.
[13:25] Evan: For start of pilot we need an on-call contact and escalation matrix.
[13:31] Nina: I'll include contacts and an escalation path in the onboarding doc.
[13:38] [14:00] -> 14 minute mark
[14:02] Marcus: A couple of edge cases: what happens if EU laws change and the provider can't legally process EU data? Who is responsible for reconfiguring?
[14:12] Amy: We include change management language; if laws change we will work through contractual remediation and provide options — typically it's a collaborative plan.
[14:20] Dr. Priya: About SSO audit: we need to know token expiration windows and whether sessions can be centrally revoked.
[14:28] Jared: Sessions honor your IdP settings; we also support session revocation via our admin APIs for emergency logout.
[14:36] Sofia: Are there any scenarios where agent tooling in the pipeline might exfiltrate data to model analysis vendors?
[14:43] Amy: No, not by default. Only managed services for model ops that you explicitly enable would have that capability.
[14:52] [15:00] <- 15 minute marker ->
[15:10] Marcus: Let's confirm the deliverables and timeline: security packet by Tue, subprocessor inventory same day, bench scheduled for Friday, pilot requirements doc by Nina.
[15:20] Amy: Correct. I'll send the security packet and SOC/ISO artifacts by Monday COB (we said Tue earlier — will confirm), subprocessor inventory right after.
[15:29] Nina: I'll open the bench ticket and propose times for 3/27.
[15:34] Jared: I'll draft the bench topology and the test plan.
[15:38] Dr. Priya: One more ask: can Redwood sign a data processing addendum with EU-specific annex?
[15:44] Amy: Yes, we have standard DPA with regional annexes; we'll share the draft.
[15:50] Sofia: Also, we may ask for a KMS escrow memo — sample wording for legal.
[15:55] Amy: We'll include a KMS escrow template in the packet.
[16:02] [16:00] -> closing segment
[16:10] Amy: Quick recap: action items — Amy to send SOC2/ISO + subprocessor inventory; Jared to set bench plan; Nina to schedule bench and provide runbook; Marcus to provide anonymized sample dataset; legal to review DPA addendum. Is that accurate?
[16:25] Dr. Priya: Yes that matches. Thanks for a clear call.
[16:30] Marcus: Thank you, talk soon.
[16:33] Amy: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and proposed times.

[End of transcript]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (Shrems spelled Shrems/Shrems II), product name typos (Dedicate vs Dedicated) — left as captured from auto-transcript.
